events.title: Objective-C created at Stepstone
events.summary: Brad Cox and Tom Love developed Objective-C circa 1984 — C with Smalltalk-style messaging and object-oriented extensions.
events.about: Objective-C adds `[object message:arg]` syntax on top of C — the language behind NeXTSTEP, macOS, and iOS until Swift. Cocoa/UIKit APIs are Objective-C (or bridged to Swift). Developers used it for iPhone apps, Mac desktop software, and NeXT workstations through Apple's 2010s transition.

narrative.whyChosen: Objective-C powered Apple's platform for two decades and bridged C systems code with OOP.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed how to layer dynamic object messaging on C without a new runtime VM — a model Swift later refined.
narrative.problemSolved: C had no objects; Smalltalk was not portable to Unix/C environments that enterprises already ran.

sources.title: HOPL IV — The Origins of Objective-C at PPI/Stepstone

events.title: Susan Kare designs Macintosh icons
events.summary: Susan Kare designed the original Macintosh icons, fonts, and UI elements in 1983–1984 — defining visual language for GUI computing.
events.about: Kare's Chicago font, trash can, and happy Mac icon made graphical interfaces legible to non-programmers. Her work influenced every desktop and mobile icon system developers design for today.

narrative.whyChosen: Kare's icons made GUIs approachable for mainstream users.
narrative.whyImportant: Visual metaphors became as important as code in human-computer interaction.
narrative.problemSolved: Early GUIs lacked consistent, memorable iconography.
